assessments.reasoning: Section 6.1.1 defines value-result calls and explicitly distinguishes the three direction modes and the omitted-direction case. It pins evaluation of the outbound l-value to the original call and the use of that l-value to the return.

challenge.method: Check the four direction conditions and compare binding the target at call time with recalculating an array-index argument after the called body changes the index. Inspect non-l-value arguments and multiple outbound operations as controls.
challenge.results: For a valid out scalar given a[i] when i is zero, a body that sets i to one and sets the out value to 9 returns 9 to the location captured at entry, a[0]. Input-only writes affect the local copy. The separate clauses reject non-l-values for out/inout and leave the order among outputs undefined, so neither justifies a stronger claim.

limitations: The claim is scoped to an ordinary same-type scalar parameter of a valid user-defined function. The example applies the documented semantics without claiming a runtime test or machine-level ABI.
